html:
Leptis Magna was a port on the coast of Libya, founded by Phoenicians and later one of the great cities of the Roman Empire. Its ruins are among the best kept of the Roman world.

It grew rich exporting olive oil and goods brought across the desert by the Garamantes. Its most famous son, Septimius Severus, born there in 145, became Roman emperor in 193 and filled his home town with a new forum, a basilica, a harbour and a triumphal arch.

After Rome, the city declined under the Vandals and Byzantines and was abandoned after the Arab conquest, and sand covered it. It became a World Heritage Site in 1982. With Cyrene and Sabratha, it is the heart of Libya's ancient past. See also Carthage.
sum: Leptis Magna was a port on the coast of Libya, founded by Phoenicians and later one of the great cities of the Roman Empire. Its ruins are among the best kept of the Roman world.
